positions.thesis: Microsoft has lagged peer performance with only 1% YTD gains despite strong recent momentum (+11% 1mo), indicating market revaluation of its AI and cloud leadership position.
evidence: The shares are up 1% over the past year and up 11% over the past month
positions.counterargument: The recent momentum may already price in most of the AI opportunity, and the stock could be vulnerable to disappointment if AI monetization slows

positions.thesis: NVIDIA remains the dominant AI infrastructure play with sustained momentum (+66% YTD, +13% 1mo), justified by its commanding position in AI chip supply.
evidence: The shares are up 66% over the past year and up 13% over the past month
positions.counterargument: Trading near yearly highs with little bad news reflected, valuation risk is significant if AI deployment slows

positions.thesis: Oracle shows accelerating momentum (+44% 1mo) even though 24% below yearly highs, suggesting strong recovery in cloud and AI adoption with reasonable valuation.
evidence: The shares are up 51% over the past year and up 44% over the past month
It is about 24% below its high of the past year, so some bad news is already reflected in the price
positions.counterargument: Execution risk on cloud transition and competition from Azure and AWS could limit gains

positions.thesis: Eli Lilly is the best-positioned company in the GLP-1 pharmaceutical revolution, benefiting from secular growth in obesity and diabetes treatment.
evidence: The shares are up 48% over the past year and up 13% over the past month
positions.counterargument: Trading near yearly highs with little bad news reflected, valuation could compress if GLP-1 market growth disappoints

positions.thesis: Intel's remarkable turnaround (+459% YTD) reflects genuine progress on foundry strategy and process node recovery, positioning it as a structural AI beneficiary.
evidence: The shares are up 459% over the past year and up 10% over the past month
positions.counterargument: Large historical underperformance suggests execution risk on foundry roadmap and competitive threats from TSMC

positions.thesis: ASML's chip equipment monopoly benefits directly from global semiconductor capacity expansion driven by AI and geopolitical diversification.
evidence: The shares are up 123% over the past year and up 14% over the past month

positions.thesis: Apple's sustained gains (+53% YTD, +9% 1mo) reflect confidence in ecosystem strength and upcoming AI-enhanced products.
evidence: The shares are up 53% over the past year and up 9% over the past month

positions.thesis: AMD's strong momentum (+361% YTD, +41% 1mo) demonstrates market confidence in its AI chip execution and data center growth.
evidence: The shares are up 361% over the past year and up 41% over the past month

positions.thesis: Broadcom benefits from semiconductor equipment and infrastructure positioning, with +92% YTD returns reflecting justified AI infrastructure demand.

positions.thesis: Johnson & Johnson offers healthcare exposure with strong dividend support and diversified pharmaceutical pipeline.
evidence: The shares are up 48% over the past year and down 1% over the past month
positions.counterargument: Mature company with limited upside if drug pipeline disappoints

positions.thesis: Micron's extraordinary +999% one-year return has pushed valuations to bubble territory with little downside priced in, making this a classic mean reversion short.
evidence: The shares are up 999% over the past year and up 91% over the past month
It is trading close to its highest point of the past year, so little bad news is currently reflected in the price
positions.counterargument: AI server demand for high-bandwidth memory is genuine and may justify sustained elevated pricing levels

positions.thesis: T-Mobile's persistent weakness (-21% YTD, -4% 1mo) despite recent industry strength suggests structural margin pressure and competitive challenges in wireless.
evidence: The shares are down 21% over the past year and down 4% over the past month
It is about 26% below its high of the past year, so some bad news is already reflected in the price
positions.counterargument: Recent stability could signal bottom if wireless market dynamics improve and TMUS cost structure becomes competitive

reasoning: The portfolio is heavily weighted toward AI and semiconductor beneficiaries (NVDA, INTC, ASML, AMD) with core positions in lagging but re-valuing tech leaders (MSFT, ORCL). Pharmaceutical growth is captured through LLY exposure. Two large short positions (MU, TMUS) represent high-conviction mean reversion and sector weakness plays. The positioning reflects confidence in AI infrastructure trends while maintaining shorts on extreme valuations.
